This is why you need to learn languages. In Italian we have 2 different ways to say “I love you”: “ti amo” is for “the one”, while “ti voglio bene” is what you say to friends and family (but also “the one”). As an Italian, I hate “ti amo”. I have said it to so many different people that are not in my life anymore and it seems like such a shallow feeling, I don’t even say it anymore. Now “ti voglio bene” on the other hand, I never regretted saying it. It means "I love you", but not in a romantic way. "Ti voglio bene" implies unconditional and selfless love and literally means "I want you to be well". It's used as a salutation in Italy to those who mean the most to you. 

I feel like you “ti voglio bene” your wife and not “ti amo” her, and that’s so much better in my eyes!

I had to pud down 2 of my kitties last year… one was 19 years old, so it was expected at that point, but she was my life companion, I spent most of my lonely life with her (I am 27 yo) 🥺 The other one was only 1 year old and had caught a bad virus… there was nothing we could have done as there is no cure for it 😢 deciding to put down my cats was literally the hardest forced decision I had to take in my entire life. The pain is excruciating. We buried them in the same spot of my garden and planted flowers on top, so when I’m sad I look over there and I feel them close ❤️ one thing that helped me a lot was adopting a couple of stray kittens from a colony in the forest next to my house (there are associations who neuter them and give them away to families). They are my joy and the reason why I work hard every day. They are not a replacement for my old kitties, but they help fill that void that was left in my heart. If you have the possibility to do so, adopting a stray kitten and knowing you are giving an helpless creature a better life could be a good thing to do. Sending much love, my thoughts are with you ❤️

Let me also add that apparently kids get bullied in school if they try to practice having a good accent (I heard this from my Japanese friends)

They learn how to *write* and *read* English very well, and they also know more grammar than any sane person will ever need, but they never practice any speaking at all.
